subject: Non-consumptive data commitment and subprocessor roadmap
messages:
From: Sara Brooks <sara.brooks@medivale.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Data use commitments for production inference

Hi David,

Thanks for the demo last week — team found the latency/cost profile compelling. Before we kick off the pilot, Legal asked for more detail about how Redwood treats inference data for production endpoints. High-level asks:

- A written commitment that Medivale production inference calls will not be used to improve public or internal models (we've been calling this a "non-consumptive processing" requirement).
- Evidence of subprocessor locations (EU/US onshore) and an inventory we can include in our DPA.
- Clarification on ownership of prompts and responses (Medivale wants exclusive rights to outputs generated from their prompts).
- Whether you can offer per-tenant toggles (so our production endpoints have learning disabled at the tenant level) vs a blanket policy.

Can you send an initial statement we can attach to the DPA and any attachments (subprocessor list, evidence pack) you can provide?

Also looping in Kevin (our counsel) in case he wants to suggest language.

Appreciate it —
Sara Brooks
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Medivale Health

(Attachment: Medivale_DPA_template_v1.pdf (pdf))

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Sara Brooks <sara.brooks@medivale.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 17:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Data use commitments for production inference

Sara — thanks for laying this out. Happy to put forward a concrete commitment and the operational evidence your team needs. Short answer up front: we can commit to non-consumptive processing for specified production inference endpoints and provide an audit trail showing that tenant-level learning is disabled.

Next steps I propose:
1) Attach a short "Non-consumptive processing addendum" to the DPA (draft attached).
2) Share our current subprocessor inventory and residency attributes (CSV attached).
3) Provide a technical note on how the per-tenant no-learning toggle works and the associated audit logs (ops note attached).

I attached: DPA_redwood_20260824.docx (draft addendum), subprocessor_inventory_20260824.csv, and a short ops note. Connor/Neha — can you review the DPA draft and the ops note? Key open items for Legal: the exact clause text for prompt/response ownership and whether we need an escrow path for derivatives.

I can do a 30 min call with your team tomorrow if that helps.

Thanks,
David Kim
Head of Privacy Partnerships
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: DPA_redwood_20260824.docx (docx); subprocessor_inventory_20260824.csv (csv))

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Brooks <sara.brooks@medivale.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:24:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Data use commitments for production inference

Thanks for the draft, David — quick legal review notes:

- Recommend explicit language: "Redwood will not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or improve models used in Redwood's public or internal model catalog, including derivative model artifacts, except as necessary to provide the Services with Customer's prior written consent."
- Add retention/appeal windows for audit logs (we hold logs for X days; Medivale may request a snapshot).
- On prompt/response ownership: propose "Customer retains all rights in prompts and generated responses produced solely in response to Customer requests; Redwood retains telemetry necessary for platform health and billing but will not assert IP rights over Customer outputs."
- Subprocessors: propose a gating clause that requires notice + 30-day objection for new subprocessors that will process Medivale's inference payloads.
- Escrow: Legal is neutral but requests product input on what an escrow of derivatives would look like operationally (SFTP export vs. on-demand export API).

Neha — any ops concerns with the proposed per-tenant toggle + audit snapshot?

Connor O'Brien
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Kevin Lawson <kevin.lawson@medivale.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Aug 2026 11:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Data use commitments for production inference

David / Connor — thanks. Attached are Medivale's redlines to your DPA draft (Medivale_DPA_redlines_v2.pdf). A few points that need clarification from Product / Ops: 

- Implementation: we prefer a per-tenant, enforceable setting that prevents any materialization of model updates using Medivale data. A broad policy language without a technical enforcement pathway won't suffice for our auditors.
- Evidence: we need a CSV of the subprocessor inventory with country and role (processing vs infra), plus an attestation signed by an officer that no on-call, downstream backups, or analytics jobs will capture inference payloads for model improvement.
- Telemetry: does Redwood collect aggregated telemetry (latency, error rates) that could indirectly be used to tune models? If so, we need a scope and retention cap.

We can accept an escrow mechanism (SFTP drop with encryption + retention window) if you provide a clear export SLA. Also please confirm whether KMS controls can be onshore for key material for Medivale's tenant.

--
Kevin Lawson
Senior Counsel, Medivale Health
(Attachment: Medivale_DPA_redlines_v2.pdf (pdf))

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Sara Brooks <sara.brooks@medivale.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Aug 2026 13:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Data use commitments for production inference

Sara / Kevin — appreciate the detailed redlines. Quick operational commitments and next steps from our side: 

- Commitment: Redwood will implement a customer-scoped non-consumptive processing regime for Medivale production inference endpoints. Concretely: per-tenant "learning_disabled" flag, enforced at the request routing layer; KV/prefix caches used only for low-latency inference are ephemeral and excluded from persistent model training pipelines.

- Audit/evidence: we will provide a subprocessor CSV (attached) with country and role, an attestation letter from our Head of Ops, and an audit snapshot of learning-disabled logs for one-week post-cutover.

- Telemetry: we collect aggregated infrastructure telemetry (latency, error rates) for platform health only; we will cap retention to 90 days for Medivale's tenant and exclude telemetry fields that could plausibly be used to reconstruct prompt/response pairs.

- Escrow/export: offer SFTP export of stored inference artifacts on demand with 30-day availability. If Medivale prefers DocuSign to finalize the DPA addendum, here is the link: https://www.docusign.com/recipient/embedded?d=abc123.

Action items:
- Connor: incorporate the clause language below into the DPA redlines (I suggest using Connor's language with the "Customer retains all rights..." sentence).
- Neha / Kimberly: prepare the attestation + subprocessor CSV and ops note (attached).
- Sara / Kevin: confirm acceptance of SFTP escrow vs. alternative.

Proposed clause (for ease of copy/paste):

"Redwood agrees that Customer Content processed through Customer-designated production inference endpoints will not be used to train, fine-tune, evaluate, or otherwise improve Redwood models or derivative models used by Redwood unless Customer provides prior written consent. Customer retains all rights in prompts and generated responses produced by those endpoints. Redwood may retain anonymized, aggregated telemetry for platform health and billing only; such telemetry will not contain prompt or response content and will be retained for no more than ninety (90) days for Customer tenants unless otherwise mutually agreed in writing."

I'll schedule a 30-min call Monday to walk through the attestation artifacts unless you'd prefer to handle via redline.

Thanks,
David Kim
Head of Privacy Partnerships
Redwood Inference
(Attachments: subprocessor_inventory_20260824.csv; DPA_redwood_20260824.docx; operations_attestation_medivale.pdf)
